headline: NEW to scans -- Saudi airstrike on a house in Asr, west Sanaa, kills 3 (preliminary toll, Ansar Allah media via AFP)
dek: A Saudi airstrike on a house in Asr, in the west of the Ansar Allah-controlled capital Sanaa, killed three people on Saturday and wounded several others, Ansar Allah media said, with the toll described as preliminary. Al-Masirah said 'the Saudi enemy targeted a house in Asr'.
sources: Ansar Allah-run Al-Masirah TV ('the Saudi enemy targeted a house in Asr'), carried by AFP
fault_line: Retaliation that deters vs retaliation that escalates: does hitting Sanaa stop the next missile at a Saudi city, or guarantee it?

sections.what_happened: A Saudi airstrike on a house in Asr, in the west of the Ansar Allah-controlled capital Sanaa, killed three people on Saturday and wounded several others, Ansar Allah media said, with the toll described as preliminary. Al-Masirah said 'the Saudi enemy targeted a house in Asr'. The strike lands the same day Saudi defences intercepted Ansar Allah missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu (totw-20261024-1500-01) and after Yemeni government warplanes struck Ansar Allah-held Mocha (totw-20261024-1500-04) — the Yemen war running in both directions on one day. SEPARATE, UNVERIFIED PARALLEL CLAIMS (not folded into the 3-killed toll): Ansar Allah spokespeople via a Times of Israel liveblog entry (14:56 , just before window) claim a Saudi strike killed 4 people from one family, including women and children, at Hiba near Taiz late last night, and a strike on a shelter for African migrants in Saada injured 7 this morning; Saudi Arabia did not respond to a request for comment on those claims. NOT the same event as Friday's Nihm-district strike (3 killed, 9 injured, same family) reported Friday — do not merge the two. No coalition comment on the Sanaa Asr strike was found in-window.
sections.what_verified: One counted publisher family: AFP (T1 wire) carrying the Al-Masirah claim. Al-Masirah/Ansar Allah media has NO declared tier in the source registry, so it is reported with attribution but does NOT count toward corroboration. CGTN also carried a 'series of Saudi airstrikes targets Sanaa' report (published 14:53 ) — CGTN has no declared tier in the registry, so it is noted as an additional carry only and is NOT counted. The Hiba/Saada claims rest on a single family (Times of Israel liveblog carrying Ansar Allah spokespeople) and are unverified.
sections.what_disputed: No coalition confirmation or denial of the Sanaa Asr strike in-window; casualty figures come solely from the Ansar Allah side via the wire carry, and the toll is explicitly preliminary. The parallel Hiba/Saada claims are single-source Ansar Allah claims with no Saudi response.
sections.why_matters: The war runs both ways in one day: hours after Ansar Allah missiles at Taif and Yanbu were intercepted, a Saudi strike hits a house in the Ansar Allah capital — the retaliation cycle, with a civilian toll both sides dispute.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (in-window, Sat Oct 24) -- Saudi airstrike on a house in Asr, west Sanaa, kills 3 (preliminary toll, Ansar Allah media via AFP); retaliation-cycle strike hours after the Taif/Yanbu missile intercepts

totw_analysis: Our read: The war runs both ways in one day: hours after Ansar Allah missiles at Taif and Yanbu were intercepted, a Saudi strike hits a house in the Ansar Allah capital — the retaliation cycle, with a civilian toll both sides dispute. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Retaliation that deters vs retaliation that escalates: does hitting Sanaa stop the next missile at a Saudi city, or guarantee it?
